questions.q: Why does LTV Global build two separate Experience Cloud sites instead of one combined portal?
options: Because Experience Cloud technically cannot support more than one user type per site
Because dealers and end customers are different populations with very different scale and needs, and a combined site would force a compromise design serving neither well
Because dealers are not allowed to use the same Salesforce org as end customers
Because Salesforce limits each org to one Experience Cloud site
questions.explain: Dealers (thousands of business users placing frequent orders) and end customers (millions of occasional individual logins) have different needs and scale; a single site would compromise both experiences.

questions.q: How does the Customer Portal's design specifically resolve Risk #4 from the Chapter 1 risk register?
options: By giving every end customer the same license type and sharing approach as dealer users
By licensing the millions of infrequent individual users under a model sized for that population, rather than reusing business-user-oriented licensing for everyone
By removing Experience Cloud entirely and handling customers by phone only
By merging the Customer Portal into the internal role hierarchy
questions.explain: Risk #4 warned about license/performance risk at millions of end-customer logins; the mitigation is sizing the Customer Portal's license type and sharing approach specifically for that population instead of a one-size-fits-all model.

questions.q: Which mechanism, established in Lesson 11, do both the Dealer Portal and Customer Portal rely on to scope each external user to their own records?
options: The internal role hierarchy
Sharing sets
Shield Platform Encryption
Criteria-based sharing rules for the global key-accounts team
questions.explain: Both portals rely on sharing sets, which scope each external user strictly to their own account relationship regardless of which portal they use, keeping the two portals' user populations isolated from each other.

questions.q: Why does this lesson reject the simpler alternative of one portal differentiated only by profiles and permission sets?
options: Because profiles cannot be used with Experience Cloud at all

Because a single site's user base and sharing configuration would still have to accommodate both populations' very different scale underneath any UI-level differentiation, reintroducing the licensing/performance risk
Because permission sets are deprecated in current Salesforce releases
Because dealer users are legally required to be on a separate site from end customers
questions.explain: Differentiating only at the profile level, within one site, wouldn't isolate the underlying scale and licensing concerns — splitting at the site level is what actually isolates one portal's scale and cost from the other's.

questions.q: Which external API from Lesson 15 does the Dealer Portal call for live pricing, and through what mechanism?
options: The credit/financing-check API, through a plain Apex callout
The shipping-carrier tracking API, through Change Data Capture
The parts-pricing/catalog API, through External Services
LedgerPoint, through a nightly batch file
questions.explain: The Dealer Portal calls the parts-pricing/catalog API through External Services, which exposes the API's schema to declarative tools so the portal can show dealers live, current pricing.
